record_type_quote: Three of these experiments also aimed to replicate the category-specific retrospective enhancement effect reported by Patil et al. and two explored the corresponding prospective memory effect.

targets.authors: Patil, A., Murty, V. P., Dunsmoor, J. E., Phelps, E. A. & Davachi, L.
targets.title: Reward retroactively enhances memory consolidation for related items.
targets.evidence_quote:
Experiment 2a replicates the design of Experiment 1 from the RREM study
6
to test retrospective memory enhancement 24-hours after encoding.
targets.outcome_quote:
The highly specific memory enhancement effect for conceptually related stimuli
6
was not replicated in our experiments using the same reward-conditioning paradigm.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall non-replication verdict governs, despite individual conditioning effects. Experiment 3 repeats the within-paper design while explicitly making a final replication attempt of the published RREM study.

targets.authors: Oyarzún, J. P., Packard, P. A., de Diego-Balaguer, R. & Fuentemilla, L.
targets.title: Motivated encoding selectively promotes memory for future inconsequential semantically-related events.
targets.evidence_quote:
In Experiment 2b, we incorporated a post-conditioning phase to examine prospective memory enhancement effects, building on prior reports of this effect induced by reward-conditioning
13
and fear-conditioning
7
.
targets.outcome_quote: Experiment 2b provided no evidence for prospective memory effects.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The prospective reward-enhancement finding is retested in the post-conditioning phases, with explicit absence of the effect in Experiments 1 and 2b. The fear-conditioning reference supplies related motivation rather than a retest of fear conditioning.

reasoning: Full publisher article and references match title, DOI and authors. New samples test published retrospective and prospective reward-memory findings. The adopted associative-learning protocol is not itself an additional target. Prospective reward target is identified by the explicit connection to reference 13, not topical similarity.
